text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- John Hardbattle, 51, leader of 'The First People of the Kalahari', an organisation he set up to fight the Botswana government for alleged unfair treatment of the Bushmen, died in a Johannesburg, South Africa, clinic on Tuesday.

- Minister of Presidential Affairs and Public Administration Ponatshego Kidikilwe, on Tuesday told students at the University of Botswana the government had no intention of releasing a report by Scotland Yard detectives into the suspected ritutal killing of a 14-year-old schoolgirl in November 1994.
- The coordinator of the exercise to eradicate cattle lung disease in the Ngamiland district of Botswana said 297,794 infected cattle had been destroyed and the exercise was in its final stages.

- The government is looking for candidates for the post of national ombudsman. The office was created in April this year, after being first mooted in a 1982 presidential report on the effect on the economy of delays in implementing government decisions.
- Senior lecturer in finance at the University of Botswana, Charles Okeahalam, called for the government to delink the Botswana unit of currency, the pula, from the South African rand.
